name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
source_notes: Verified against the OWASP GenAI-Security-Project/GenAI-LLM-Top10 repo (2026/final, commit 9253e38) including Appendix A CWE mappings.
caveats: The repo gives the release date as 2026-08-04; the genai.owasp.org landing page shows 2026-08-03.
A secondary news site published an incorrect 2026 list (e.g. "Insecure Output Handling", "Vector and Memory Flaws"); ignore it.
CWE lists are the primary (●) mappings from Appendix A; LLM08 CWE-798 is a secondary (○) mapping and LLM07 CWE-494 comes from the Appendix A slopsquatting note.
LLM08:2026 replaces and broadens LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage; it explicitly excludes client-side bundle inspection, so API keys in client bundles map to LLM02:2026.
Maturity 'lab' reflects the legacy owasp.org LLM Top 10 project entry (level 3, label inferred); the list itself is maintained by the OWASP GenAI Security Project.
detection.static entries are reinhardt rule ideas inferred from the OWASP text, not OWASP-published detections; AI SDK helper names (e.g. stepCountIs) are unverified.
related ASI links come from the OWASP Appendix A LLM-to-ASI crosswalk unless prefixed (inferred).

items.name: Prompt Injection
items.summary: Crafted content changes model behavior in unintended ways; the 2026 scope covers direct input, retrieved content, tool output, image/audio/video, intermediate reasoning and persistent memory, and notes there is no clean equivalent of parameterized queries.
prevention: Constrain the model's role and capabilities and require a strict output schema that trusted code (not a second LLM) validates.
Keep credentials and state-changing capability in application code, with least privilege per operation.
Route external content through a separate provenance-labeled channel and filter at every modality boundary.
Strip invisible Unicode (tag-block, variation-selector, zero-width) at ingest and render boundaries.
Require human confirmation for privileged, irreversible or externally visible actions, and treat memory writes as privileged.
Pin, sign and verify MCP servers and tool packages, audit tool descriptions, and test adaptively.

static: User input (req.body, searchParams) concatenated or templated into the system message instead of a separate user-role message
Fetched web/RAG/file content inserted into the prompt without delimiting or provenance labeling
No stripping of tag-block (U+E0000-E007F), variation-selector (U+FE00-FE0F) or zero-width (U+200B-U+200D, U+2060) characters before prompt assembly or rendering
MCP config (mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json) running packages via npx -y without a version pin or with @latest
MCP filesystem server rooted at / or ~, or tokens inlined in the MCP server env block
review: Apply the 'Rule of Two': flag flows that combine untrusted input, sensitive data and state change or external communication.
Audit tool and MCP descriptions for hidden instructions.

items.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
items.summary: Personal data, secrets or proprietary information leak through model inputs, outputs, retrieval, logs or traces.
prevention: Minimize the context sent to external model providers.
Authorize retrieval inside the index query, before results reach the model.
Never place secrets, credentials or regulated data in system prompts.
Detect sensitive data with classifiers rather than regex alone, and apply per-user query budgets.
Scrub logs and traces before APM ingestion; gate log-probabilities and redact reasoning traces.

static: new OpenAI({ dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true }) or new Anthropic({ dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true }) in client code
Public-prefixed AI key env names: NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY, EXPO_PUBLIC_*_API_KEY, REACT_APP_OPENAI_API_KEY
Literal sk-... / sk-ant-... keys in 'use client' files or other client bundles
console.log(messages) or logging of full prompts/completions to third-party APM/observability
review: Which user/regulated data is sent to which model provider

items.name: Excessive Agency
items.summary: An LLM-driven system can take damaging actions because it has excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy.
prevention: Minimize the number of tools and the functionality each exposes; avoid open-ended tools such as shell or arbitrary URL fetch.
Give every tool a strict input schema and validate arguments before use.
Grant tools minimal permissions (e.g. a read-only DB identity) and execute in the user's context with minimal OAuth scope.
Require user approval for impactful actions and enforce authorization in code (complete mediation), not by the model.
Limit damage with tool-use monitoring, rate limits and circuit breakers.

static: Tool definitions (tool({...}), tools: [...], LangChain DynamicTool, MCP server.tool(...)) whose execute calls exec/spawn/fs.writeFile/fs.rm or arbitrary fetch with model-chosen arguments and no allowlist
Tool input schemas that accept a free-form command or path (e.g. z.string() for a shell command or file path)
Destructive tools (delete/send/pay/transfer) with no confirmation or human-approval step
Admin/service-role DB credentials (e.g. Supabase service_role key) used inside AI tool routes
Authorization expressed only in prompt text (e.g. 'only admins may...') with no code check before the tool runs
review: Tool inventory and scope versus actual need
Preservation of user scope across chained agents

items.name: Supply Chain
items.summary: Third-party models, datasets, adapters, packages, tools and MCP servers can be vulnerable or malicious; the 2026 scope adds trust failures in promoted artifacts.
prevention: Maintain an SBOM/AIBOM for models and components.
Use signed models and verify hashes.
Pin, sign and verify every MCP server and third-party tool package.
Apply standard vulnerable-and-outdated-component practices to AI dependencies.

static: MCP config (mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json) running packages via npx -y without a version pin or with @latest
MCP filesystem server rooted at / or ~, or tokens inlined in the MCP server env block
trust_remote_code=True, torch.load / pickle.load of downloaded models, or unpinned Hugging Face model revisions
review: Provenance of models, adapters and datasets promoted into production

items.name: Data and Model Poisoning
items.summary: Pre-training, fine-tuning or embedding data, or model artifacts, are manipulated to introduce backdoors, bias or vulnerabilities; 2026 folds in fine-tuning subversion.
prevention: Treat chat templates, tokenizer configs, LoRA/PEFT adapters and quantization artifacts as security-relevant code.

static: trust_remote_code=True, torch.load / pickle.load of downloaded models, or unpinned Hugging Face model revisions

items.name: Unbounded Consumption
items.summary: Uncontrolled inference leads to denial of service, runaway cost (denial of wallet) or model extraction; 2026 adds reasoning-token exhaustion, multimodal cost, agent-tool loops and MCP fan-out.
prevention: Enforce tokens-per-minute and per-day limits with pre-flight token estimation.
Set hard spending caps that halt inference.
Add agent circuit breakers: step, recursion-depth, time and per-run cost limits, with state hashing to detect loops.
Require authentication on all inference endpoints.
Monitor cost attribution continuously.

static: LLM calls with no max_tokens / maxOutputTokens / max_completion_tokens
Agent loops with no step cap (AI SDK stopWhen step-count condition, LangChain maxIterations)
AI API routes with no rate-limit middleware
Public AI API route with no auth check (open proxy to a paid model)
new OpenAI({ dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true }) or new Anthropic({ dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true }) in client code
Public-prefixed AI key env names: NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY, EXPO_PUBLIC_*_API_KEY, REACT_APP_OPENAI_API_KEY
Literal sk-... / sk-ant-... keys in 'use client' files or other client bundles
review: Spending caps and cost alerts configured at the provider

items.name: Misinformation
items.summary: The model produces false or misleading output (including hallucinated package names) that people or systems act on.
prevention: Separate generation from execution (Claim-Check-Act).
Validate tool calls: arguments, authorization and preconditions before acting.

static: package.json dependencies that do not exist on the registry or are newly published (hallucinated package names / slopsquatting; needs a registry lookup)
review: Human verification of model claims used in decisions

items.name: Hidden Context Exposure
items.summary: Hidden context (system prompt, developer instructions, retrieved policy text, tool/function schemas incl. MCP tool descriptions) is revealed; severity is high when it embeds credentials or when authorization relies on it staying secret.
prevention: Do not put credentials, connection strings, tokens or other sensitive data in hidden context.
Use deterministic guardrails rather than prompt instructions.
Enforce authorization independently of the LLM.

static: Secret-looking values (API keys, DB URLs, passwords, tokens) interpolated into system / role:'system' strings or instructions
Credentials embedded in tool/function schemas or MCP tool descriptions
Authorization expressed only in prompt text (e.g. 'only admins may...') with no code check before the tool runs
review: Whether any security decision depends on the secrecy of the prompt

items.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
items.summary: Weaknesses in how embeddings and vector stores are built, stored and queried (e.g. in RAG) allow data leakage across users, poisoning or manipulation.
prevention: Apply permission-aware access control to vector retrieval.
Validate data, authenticate sources and track provenance.
Segregate data by trust tier.
Use anomaly detection and monitoring.
Manage the storage lifecycle of embeddings.

static: Vector queries with no tenant/user filter (e.g. similaritySearch(q) with no filter)
Model output persisted to long-term memory or a vector store without validation or per-user namespacing
review: Tenant isolation design of the vector store

items.name: Improper Output Handling
items.summary: Model output reaches downstream interpreters (shell, eval, HTML/Markdown, SQL, file paths, terminals) without validation or encoding; 2026 adds ANSI/OSC escapes, Markdown-image exfiltration and insecure AI-generated code.
prevention: Treat model output as untrusted (zero trust) and apply ASVS-style validation.
Use context-aware output encoding and parameterized queries.
Deploy a strict CSP and strip control characters before writing to terminals or logs.
Disable auto-rendering of Markdown images, previews and iframes by default, or allowlist/proxy them.
Do not auto-deploy LLM-generated code without review.

static: Model output (completion.choices[0].message.content, result.text, toolCall.args) flowing into eval, new Function, vm.runIn*, child_process.exec/execSync or spawn(..., {shell:true})
Model output written to innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, document.write, or a Markdown renderer with raw HTML enabled (e.g. rehype-raw, marked without a sanitizer)
Model output used in raw SQL ($queryRawUnsafe, sequelize.query(str), string-built db.query)
Model output used in fs paths / path.join without normalization, or as a fetch(url) target (SSRF)
Chat UI auto-rendering model Markdown images or link previews without a URL allowlist (exfiltration via query string)
review: Pipelines that deploy or execute AI-generated code without review
